STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r4.claim: After recalling worldly blessings, the surah tells of Noah's struggle against his people's denial and rebuke and his journey in the ark.
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r4.anchor: the sūrah narrates the story of Noah, his struggles with the denial and rebuke of his people, and his journey in the ark (vv. 23–41)

STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.claim: The opposition of affluent and powerful people to prophets recurs throughout this surah, as elsewhere in the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.anchor: The opposition to prophets by the affluent and powerful is a recurrent theme in this sūrah

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p559/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p559/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p559/r5.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects al-Zamakhsharī's claim that إذا lies in the conditional apodosis: it falls between إنكم and its predicate, while that clause answers an omitted oath.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p559/r5.anchor: وليس إذا واقعا في جزاء الشرط بل واقعا بين إنكم والخبر وإنكم والخبر ليس جزاء للشرط

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p559/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p559/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p559/r6.claim: If إنكم and its predicate answered the conditional, they would need an initial fāʾ; Basran grammarians reject the construction without it, though al-Farrāʾ allows it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p559/r6.anchor: ولو كانت إنكم والخبر جوابا للشرط للزمت الفاء في إنكم بل لو كان بالفاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p559/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p559/r7.speaker: سيبويه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p559/r7.claim: Sībawayh takes the second أنكم as an emphatic substitute for the first; the first clause's omitted predicate is supplied by the second and governs إذا.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p559/r7.anchor: والمنقول عن سيبويه أن أنكم بدل من الأولى وفيها معنى التأكيد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p559/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p559/r8.speaker: الفراء والجرمي والمبرد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p559/r8.claim: Al-Farrāʾ, al-Jarmī, and al-Mubarrad treat the second أنكم as repetition for emphasis; مخرجون is the first clause's predicate and governs إذا.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p559/r8.anchor: وذهب الفراء والجرمي والمبرد إلى أن أنكم الثانية كررت للتأكيد لما طال الكلام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p559/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p559/r9.speaker: المبرد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p559/r9.claim: Al-Mubarrad rejects the substitution analysis because the first أن has no separately stated future predicate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p559/r9.anchor: وكان المبرد يأبى البدل لكونه من غير مستقبل إذ لم يذكر خبر إن الأولى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p559/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p559/r10.speaker: الأخفش
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p559/r10.claim: Al-Akhfash parses أنكم مخرجون as a verbal noun raised by an omitted verb meaning your being brought out occurs; the conditional clause may be its predicate, or the omitted verb may be the first clause's predicate and govern إذا.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p559/r10.anchor: وذهب الأخفش إلى أن أنكم مخرجون مقدر بمصدر مرفوع

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p560/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p560/r1.speaker: المبرد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p560/r1.claim: Al-Mubarrad's analysis repeats أنكم for emphasis, places an adverb between its occurrences, and makes مخرجون the first clause's predicate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p560/r1.anchor: ثنى أنكم للتوكيد، وحسن ذلك الفصل ما بين الأول والثاني بالظرف ومخرجون خبر عن الأول وهذا قول المبرد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p560/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p560/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p560/r2.claim: Abū Ḥayyān calls al-Zamakhsharī's alternative parse straightforward and free of strain: the second clause is a subject-predicate construction meaning their being raised when they die.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p560/r2.anchor: أو جعل أنكم مخرجون مبتدأ وإذا متم خبرا على معنى إخراجكم إذا متم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p560/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p560/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p560/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī also proposes raising أنكم مخرجون with a verb that serves as the conditional result, as if to say that when they die their being brought out occurs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p560/r3.anchor: أو رفع أنكم مخرجون بفعل هو جزاء الشرط كأنه قيل إذا متم وقع إخراجكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p560/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p560/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p560/r4.claim: That last parse is al-Akhfash's view; Abū Ḥayyān allows either that the conditional clause predicates the first أنكم or that the omitted verb does so and governs إذا.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p560/r4.anchor: وهذا قول الأخفش إلا أنه حتم أن تكون الجملة الشرطية خبرا عن أنكم ونحن جوزنا في قول الأخفش هذا الوجه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p560/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p560/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p560/r5.claim: A reading attributed to ʿAbd Allāh omits the first أنكم, reading the question as أيعدكم إذا متم.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p560/r5.anchor: وفي قراءة عبد الله أيعدكم إذا متم بإسقاط أنكم الأولى

TABATABAI:23:23-54/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:23:23-54/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:23:23-54/r3.claim: Their question about being brought out after becoming soil and bones refers to resurrection from graves for reckoning and recompense.
TABATABAI:23:23-54/r3.anchor: للحساب والجزاء { هيهات هيهات لما توعدون }

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكونفيهأنبدلامنشيءليسبال.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكونفيهأنبدلامنشيءليسبال.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكونفيهأنبدلامنشيءليسبال.claim: In 23:35, أنكم مخرجون replaces the preceding clause about dying and becoming dust and bones; the first أن is fronted to identify the event before resurrection.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكونفيهأنبدلامنشيءليسبال.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكونفيهأنبدلامنشيءليسبال.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكونفيهأنبدلامنشيءليسبال.claim: The same substitution appears in prose with a conditional clause before a second أن; the second clause supplies the promised action.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكونفيهأنبدلامنشيءليسبال.anchor: أنه إذا أتاك أنه سيفعل وقد علمت

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكونفيهأنبدلامنشيءليسبال.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكونفيهأنبدلامنشيءليسبال.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكونفيهأنبدلامنشيءليسبال.claim: إن cannot begin independently in this construction as nouns or verbs can; it must remain attached to the preceding statement.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكونفيهأنبدلامنشيءليسبال.anchor: لأن إن لا تبتدأ في كل موضع

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكونفيهأنبدلامنشيءليسبال.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكونفيهأنبدلامنشيءليسبال.speaker: ابن مقبل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكونفيهأنبدلامنشيءليسبال.claim: Ibn Muqbil's verse supports the construction in which a conditional clause is followed by a second أن clause giving the consequence.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابتكونفيهأنبدلامنشيءليسبال.anchor: وسمعناهم يقولون في قول ابن مقبل

SAMIN-DURR:23:35/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:35/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:35/r1.claim: First analysis: the first anna has an omitted noun annexed to the address pronoun, with that pronoun standing in its place; its predicate is the if-clause, and the second anna repeats it to clarify the omission.
SAMIN-DURR:23:35/r1.anchor: مضاف لضمير الخطاب حذف وأقيم المضاف إليه مقامه

SAMIN-DURR:23:35/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:35/r2.speaker: الجرمي والمبرد والفراء
SAMIN-DURR:23:35/r2.claim: The second analysis makes makhrajūn the predicate of the first anna and governor of idhā; the second anna repeats the first after a long separation.

SAMIN-DURR:23:35/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:35/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:35/r3.claim: Third analysis: the second anna-clause is a nominative verbal noun; an omitted verb is the conditional answer to idhā, and that answer plus the if-clause predicates the first anna.
SAMIN-DURR:23:35/r3.anchor: ذلك الفعل المحذوف هو جواب " إذا " الشرطية

SAMIN-DURR:23:35/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:35/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:35/r4.claim: Fourth analysis also treats the second anna-clause as a verbal noun raised by an omitted verb, but that verb itself predicates the first anna and governs idhā.
SAMIN-DURR:23:35/r4.anchor: إلا أن هذا الفعل المقدر خبر ل " أن " الأولى

SAMIN-DURR:23:35/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:35/r5.speaker: سيبويه
SAMIN-DURR:23:35/r5.claim: Sībawayh omits the first anna's predicate, estimated as your resurrection; it governs the time phrase, and the second anna-clause is an apposition to the first.
SAMIN-DURR:23:35/r5.anchor: بدل من الأولى، وهذا مذهب سيبويه

SAMIN-DURR:23:35/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:35/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:35/r6.claim: Sixth analysis treats the second anna-clause as a subject with the time phrase as its fronted predicate; the whole clause predicates the first anna.
SAMIN-DURR:23:35/r6.anchor: أن { أنكم مخرجون } مبتدأ، وخبره الظرف مقدما عليه

SAMIN-DURR:23:35/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:35/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:35/r7.claim: Makhrajūn cannot govern idhā, because material governed by anna cannot govern material before it; mat tum also cannot govern it because it is genitive as the complement of muḍāf.
SAMIN-DURR:23:35/r7.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يكون العامل في " إذا " " مخرجون " على كل قول

SAMIN-DURR:23:35/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:23:35/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:23:35/r8.claim: The anna-clause is accusative or genitive after omission of its original preposition, though Arabic also permits it without a preposition in the accusative.
SAMIN-DURR:23:35/r8.anchor: و " أنكم " وما في حيزه في محل نصب أو جر بعد حذف الحرف

ZAJJAJ:v4p349/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p349/r8.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p349/r8.claim: The repeated أنكم in 23:35 is a parallel case of repeating a clause element after a long intervening phrase.
ZAJJAJ:v4p349/r8.anchor: ومثله (أيعدكم أنكم إذا متم وكنتم ترابا وعظاما أنكم مخرجون

ASAD-NOTES:23:33/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:23:33/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:23:33/r2.claim: They dismiss the messenger as an ordinary human and reject his promise that people will be raised after becoming dust and bones.
ASAD-NOTES:23:33/r2.anchor: nothing but a mortal like yourselves

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p123/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p123/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p123/r1.claim: He calls the passage's close with resurrection natural: resurrection is the final link in the sequence of life and its development.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p123/r1.anchor: فأنتَ ترى أن ختام الآيات هذه بالبعث، هو الختمُ الطبيعي، وهو الحلقة النهائية في سلسلة الحياة وتطورها

QIRAAT-ER:23:35:4#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:23:35:4#1/r1.speaker: canonical
QIRAAT-ER:23:35:4#1/r1.claim: The segment identifies mittum with kasra on mīm as the standard canonical Form I perfect of the root m-w-t.
QIRAAT-ER:23:35:4#1/r1.anchor: canonical, mutawatir: Standard canonical reading with kasra on mīm: mittum — Form I perfect of m-w-t

QIRAAT-ER:23:35:4#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:23:35:4#2/r1.speaker: vw
QIRAAT-ER:23:35:4#2/r1.claim: The canonical variant muttum has ḍamma on mīm, an alternate vocalization of the same root; both forms are accepted.
QIRAAT-ER:23:35:4#2/r1.anchor: vw, mutawatir: Canonical variant with ḍamma on mīm: muttum — alternate voweling of the same root

ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r1.claim: The opening resumes the preceding rebuke: the deniers reject and deem impossible the resurrection that the Prophet calls them to believe in.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r1.anchor: استئناف لتقرير ما قبله من زجرهم عن اتباعه عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r2.claim: The first أنكم may be construed with an implicit preposition (بأنكم), though the preposition may also be unexpressed.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r2.anchor: على تقدير حرف الجر أي بأنكم ويجوز أن لا يقدر نحو وعدتك الخير

ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r3.claim: The standard kasra on mīm follows مات يمات; another reading has ḍamma, following مات يموت.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r3.anchor: بكسر الميم من مات يمات وقريء بضمها من مات يموت

ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r4.claim: One explanation is that former flesh and similar parts become dust, while others become bare, decayed bones; dust comes first because its transformation is especially implausible and it derives from visible parts.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r4.anchor: وكان بعض أجزائكم من اللحم ونظائره ترابا وبعضها عظاما نخرة

ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r5.claim: Alternatively, earlier generations were wholly dust, while later generations are bones.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r5.anchor: أو وكان متقدموكم ترابا صرفا ومتأخروكم عظاما

ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r6.claim: The second أنكم reinforces the first after the long separation from its predicate مخرجون.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r6.anchor: تأكيد لأنكم الأول ولطول الفصل بينه وبين خبره

ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r7.claim: The promised outcome is that they will emerge alive from their graves as before, after dying and becoming dust.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r7.anchor: أي أيعدكم أنكم مخرجون من قبوركم أحياء كما كنتم أولا

ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r8.speaker: الفراء والجرمي والمبرد
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r8.claim: They attach إذا to مخرجون; this does not mean emergence occurs at the instant of death, despite Abu Nizar's objection, which al-Sakhawi refutes and al-Suyuti transmits.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r8.anchor: واختار هذا الإعراب الفراء والجرمي والمبرد ولا يلزم من ذلك كون الإخراج وقت الموت

ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r9.speaker: سيبويه
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r9.claim: Sibawayh treats the second أنكم as an emphatic بدل of the first; the first predicate is omitted, inferred from the second, and governs إذا. An adverb of time cannot directly predicate of a person unless إخراجكم is understood.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r9.anchor: وفيه معنى التأكيد وخبر أن الأولى محذوف لدلالة خبر الثانية عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r10.speaker: المبرد
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r10.claim: Al-Mubarrad objects to Sibawayh's بدل analysis because it lacks an independent constituent: the first أن has no stated predicate.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r10.anchor: وكان المبرد يأبى البدل لكونه من غير مستقل إذ لم يذكر خبر أن الأولى

ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r11.speaker: الأخفش
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r11.claim: Al-Akhfash derives مخرجون from an omitted يحدث: either the conditional clause predicates the first أن and the omitted verb answers إذا, or that verb is the predicate and governs إذا; another attribution makes أنكم مخرجون the subject of إذا.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p30#3/r11.anchor: وذهب الأخفش إلى أن ( أنكم مخرجون ) مقدر بمصدر مرفوع بفعل محذوف

ALUSI-FULL:v18p31/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p31/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p31/r1.claim: Another parsing makes أنكم مخرجون the subject and إذا متم its predicate, with the clause serving as predicate of the first أن; al-Baḥr calls this easy, and al-Sakhawi attributes it to al-Mubarrad.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p31/r1.anchor: أن يكون ( أنكم مخرجون ) مبتدأ و ( إذا متم ) خبرا

ALUSI-FULL:v18p31/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p31/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p31/r2.claim: Al-Alusi prefers the parsing reported from al-Farra and his associates as best suited to the Qur'anic word order.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p31/r2.anchor: والذي يقتضيه جزالة النظم الكريم ما ذكرناه عن الفراء ومن معه

ALUSI-FULL:v18p31/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p31/r3.speaker: عبد الله
ALUSI-FULL:v18p31/r3.claim: The reading attributed to ʿAbd Allah omits the first أنكم and reads أيعدكم إذا متم.
ALUSI-FULL:v18p31/r3.anchor: وفي قراءة عبد الله ( أيعدكم إذا متم ) بإسقاط ( أنكم ) الأولى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417/r5.claim: The second anna is repeated because the intervening phrase has become long; the sense is whether they are promised that after dying and becoming dust and bones they will be brought out.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417/r5.anchor: وأعاد "أنكم" لما طال الكلام، ومعنى الكلام: أيعدكم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417/r6.speaker: عبد الله
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417/r6.claim: The reading attributed to Abdullah omits the repeated anna, and Baghawi cites the verse about whoever opposes God and His Messenger as a parallel construction.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p417/r6.anchor: وكذلك هو في قراءة عبد الله، نظيره في القرآن: "ألم يعلموا أنه من يحادد الله ورسوله

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:34-36/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:34-36/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:34-36/r3.claim: They picture bodies reduced to earth and bones stripped of flesh and sinews.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:34-36/r3.anchor: مجردة عن اللحوم والأعصاب. { أنكم مخرجون }

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:34-36/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:34-36/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:34-36/r4.claim: Being brought out may mean resurrection from graves or being recreated from nonexistence into existence.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:34-36/r4.anchor: من الأجداث أو من العدم تارة أخرى إلى الوجود،

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:34-36/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:34-36/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:34-36/r5.claim: The repeated anna may reinforce the first after a long separation from its predicate; other parses make the second a new subject with an advanced predicate, conditional answer, or clause explaining the first.
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:34-36/r5.anchor: و { أنكم } تكرير للأول أكد به لما طال الفصل بينه وبين خبره

BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r11.claim: They describe death as souls separating from bodies, with dust covering the flesh beneath the bones until only bare bones remain.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r12.claim: The second “that you will be brought out” replaces the first “that you” to clarify what is promised after their souls have been stirred by the preceding description.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r12.anchor: مبدلا من { أنكم } الأولى إيضاحا للمعنى

BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r13.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r13.claim: Being brought out means leaving that state and returning to life in the bodies they had before.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p199/r13.anchor: أي من تلك الحالة التي صرتم إليها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p52#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p52#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p52#2/r4.claim: أيعدكم is an astonished question that shifts their attack from his claim to be a messenger to the message he conveys.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p53/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p53/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p53/r1.claim: The promise is that they will be brought out of their graves after death and bodily disintegration, alive with a complete human form for resurrection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p53/r1.anchor: مفعول { يعدكم } أي يعدكم إخراج مخرج إياكم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p53/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p53/r2.speaker: الجرمي والمبرد
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p53/r2.claim: Al-Jarmī and al-Mubarrad allow the second أنكم to repeat the first after an intervening clause, adding emphasis to the improbably phrased promise.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p53/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p53/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p53/r3.claim: Another possible parsing makes the second أنكم the subject, with the إذا clause as its fronted predicate; that whole clause then predicates the first أنكم.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p53/r3.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون { أنكم مخرجون } مبتدأ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p53/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p53/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p53/r4.claim: The deniers treat death and reduction to dust and bones as states incompatible with life and restoration of the human body, which fuels their incredulity.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p53/r4.anchor: وجعلوا موجب الاستبعاد هو حصول أحوال تنافي أنهم مبعوثون بحسب قصور عقولهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p53/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p53/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p53/r5.claim: هيهات explains the preceding promise and is therefore a separate, uncoordinated sentence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p53/r5.anchor: وجملة { هيهات } بيان لجملة { يعدكم } فلذلك فصلت ولم تعطف

BURSEVI:v6p58#4/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p58#4/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p58#4/r7.claim: They ask whether the prophet is promising them resurrection.
BURSEVI:v6p58#4/r7.anchor: ايا وعده ميدهد شمارا اين يغمبر

BURSEVI:v6p58#4/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p58#4/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p58#4/r8.claim: The mīm in mittum is read with kasra from māta-yamātu or with damma from māta-yamūtu.
BURSEVI:v6p58#4/r8.anchor: بكسر الميم من مات يمات وقرىء بضمها من مات يموت

BURSEVI:v6p58#4/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p58#4/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p58#4/r9.claim: They imagine themselves as dust and bare bones stripped of flesh and sinews; dust comes first because its transformation is more implausible, or because earlier people were dust and later ones bones.
BURSEVI:v6p58#4/r9.anchor: نخرة مجردة عن اللحوم والأعصاب أي كان بعض أجزائكم من اللحم ونظائره

BURSEVI:v6p58#4/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p58#4/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p58#4/r10.claim: Bursevi prefers that they mean becoming bones and then dust, since wāw merely joins without fixing the order.
BURSEVI:v6p58#4/r10.anchor: الظاهر أن مرادهم بيان صيرورتهم عظاما ثم ترابا لأن الواو لمطلق الجمع

BURSEVI:v6p58#5/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p58#5/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p58#5/r1.claim: Innakum repeats the earlier assertion for emphasis after a long separation from its predicate, mukhrajun.
BURSEVI:v6p58#5/r1.anchor: تأكيد للأول لطول الفصل بينه وبين خبره

BURSEVI:v6p58#5/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p58#5/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p58#5/r2.claim: They would be brought alive out of their graves as they were before.
BURSEVI:v6p58#5/r2.anchor: أي من القبور أحياء كما كنتم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p143/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p143/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p143/r1.claim: The question challenges the hearers to confront the promise as implausible and mocks it.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p143/r1.anchor: قوله أيعدكم استفهام بمعنى التوقيف على جهة الاستبعاد وبمعنى الهزء بهذا الوعد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p143/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p143/r2.speaker: سيبويه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p143/r2.claim: Sibawayh treats the second “annakum” as a substitute for the first, reinforcing it and repeating it because the sentence is long.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p143/r2.anchor: وأنكم الثانية بدل من الأولى عند سيبويه وفيه معنى تأكيد الأولى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p143/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p143/r3.speaker: المبرد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p143/r3.claim: Al-Mubarrad objects to calling it substitution because the first “anna” clause is not independent without its predicate.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p143/r3.anchor: وكأن المبرد أبى عبارة البدل لكونه من غير مستقل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p143/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p143/r4.speaker: سيبويه
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p143/r4.claim: Sibawayh supplies an omitted predicate, “you will be resurrected after death”; that clause governs “when.”
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p143/r4.anchor: والخبر عند سيبويه محذوف تقديره أنكم تبعثون إذا متم، وهذا المقدر هو العامل في إذا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p143/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p143/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p143/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿūd's reading omits the first “annakum” and places “when you die” directly before the resurrection clause.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p143/r5.anchor: وفي قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود «أيعدكم إذا متم وكنتم ترابا وعظاما أنكم مخرجون»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p143/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p143/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p143/r6.claim: Being brought out means resurrection from the graves.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p471#5/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p471#5/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p471#5/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj parses the first that-clause as the object of the promise, with the sense: does he promise that you will be brought out when you die? The repeated that follows the long clause.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p471#5/r1.anchor: قال الزجاج موضع أنكم نصب على معنى أيعدكم أنكم مخرجون إذا متم فلما طال الكلام أعيد ذكر أن

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p474#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p474#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p474#2/r3.claim: They deny meeting God at the Resurrection and bodily resurrection, mocking the promise that dead people reduced to dust and bones will be brought out again as impossibly remote.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p474#2/r3.anchor: وقالوا {أيعدكم أنكم إذا متم وكنتم ترابا وعظاما أنكم مخرجون. هيهات هيهات لما توعدون} أي: بعيد بعيد ذلك.

JISHUMI:v7p5046/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5046/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5046/r3.claim: One analysis makes مخرجون the predicate of the first أنكم, with the second أنكم repeated for emphasis.
JISHUMI:v7p5046/r3.anchor: قلنا: فيه قولان: أولهما: مخرجون، وتكون الثانية مكررة للتأكيد

JISHUMI:v7p5046/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5046/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5046/r4.claim: A second analysis takes the whole clause as the predicate, with an understood إخراجكم.
JISHUMI:v7p5046/r4.anchor: وثانيهما: أن يكون الخبر الجملة بتقدير

JISHUMI:v7p5046/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5046/r17.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5046/r17.claim: The deniers say the messenger promises they will be brought alive from their graves after becoming dust and bones.
JISHUMI:v7p5046/r17.anchor: أيعدكم هذا الرسول أنكم إذا متم وكنتم ترابا وعظاما

JISHUMI:v7p5046/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5046/r18.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p5046/r18.claim: Repeating أنكم after a long clause has a parallel in the wording of 4:14.
JISHUMI:v7p5046/r18.anchor: وأعاد أنكم لما طال الكلام، ونظيره: (ألم يعلموا أنه من يحادد الله ورسوله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p188#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p188#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p188#2/r1.claim: The repeated innakum emphasizes the statement, made apt by the intervening time adverb; mukhrajūn may predicate the first innakum, or the second clause may be parsed as a nominal clause or conditional result.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p188#2/r1.anchor: { إنكم } للتوكيد ، وحسن ذلك لفصل ما بين الأول والثاني بالظرف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p188#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p188#2/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p188#2/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿūd’s reading omits the first innakum and reads “Does he promise you, when you have died…”.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p188#2/r2.anchor: وفي قراءة ابن مسعود : ( أيعدكم إذا متم )

MUQATIL:23:35-37/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:23:35-37/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:23:35-37/r1.claim: Hud's promise is that they will be brought out of the earth alive after death.
MUQATIL:23:35-37/r1.anchor: { أيعدكم } هود { أنكم إذا متم وكنتم ترابا وعظاما أنكم مخرجون } [آية: 35] من الأرض أحياء بعد الموت

NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#2/r1.claim: Nafi, Hamza, Ali, and Hafs read “you die” with kasra; the other readers use ḍamma.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#2/r1.anchor: ﴿ أيعدكم أنكم إذا متم ﴾ بالكسر نافع وحمزة وعلى حفص وغيرهم بالضم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#2/r2.claim: They are being promised resurrection for questioning, reckoning, reward, and punishment.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#2/r3.claim: Repeating “that you” adds emphasis; the intervening time phrase makes the repetition acceptable.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#2/r3.anchor: وثنى انكم للتأكيد وحسن ذلك للفصل بين الأول والثانى بالظرف

NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#2/r4.claim: “Brought forth” predicates the first “that you”; the sense is “Does he promise that you will be brought forth when you have died and become dust and bones?”
NASAFI-FULL:v3p122#2/r4.anchor: ومخرجون خبر عن الأول والتقدير أيعدكم أنكم مخرجون إذا متم وكنتم ترابا وعظاما

QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r8.claim: The promise they deride is that after death and becoming dust and bones they will be raised from their graves.

QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r9.speaker: سيبويه
QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r9.claim: Sibawayh treats the first anna as the object of yaʿidukum and the second anna as its بدل.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r9.anchor: والثانية بدل منها هذا مذهب سيبويه

QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r10.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r10.claim: Al-Farra cites Abdullah's reading without the first anna, comparing its syntax to “I think, if you leave, that you will regret it.”
QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r10.anchor: قال الفراء: وفي قراءة عبد الله «أيعدكم إذا متم وكنتم ترابا وعظاما أنكم مخرجون»

QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r11.speaker: الفراء والجرمي وأبو العباس المبرد
QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r11.claim: Al-Farra, al-Jurmi, and al-Mubarrad treat the second anna as a repetition for emphasis, made fitting by the sentence's length.
QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r11.anchor: إلى أن الثانية مكررة للتوكيد، لما طال الكلام

QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r12.speaker: الأخفش
QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r12.claim: Al-Akhfash understands “your being raised” as an event that will occur; the second anna is nominative under an implicit verb, like saying “today, the battle.”
QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r12.anchor: وقال الأخفش: المعنى أيعدكم أنكم إذا متم وكنتم ترابا وعظاما يحدث إخراجكم

QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r13.speaker: أبو إسحاق
QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r13.claim: Abu Ishaq allows reading both particles with kasra, since yaʿidukum can mean “does he say to you.”
QURTUBI-FULL:23:33-35/r13.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: ويجوز «أيعدكم إنكم إذا متم وكنتم ترابا وعظاما إنكم مخرجون»

RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r9.claim: Their resurrection objection asks whether they will be returned alive after death and decomposition in order to be recompensed.

RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r10.claim: After asking whether resurrection will occur, they intensify their denial with the expression meaning how far-fetched.
RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r10.anchor: { هيهات هيهات لما توعدون } ثم أكدوا

RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r13.claim: God does not answer these objections in this passage because their errors are evident; omnipotence and knowledge entail His ability to resurrect.

RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r14.claim: Without resurrection, the strong could oppress the weak without redress, which is unfitting for the Wise God; the Qurʾān says each soul will be recompensed for its striving.
RAZI-FULL:v23p85#2/r14.anchor: تسليط القوى على الضعيف في الدنيا ظلما

RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r1.claim: The repeated anna in the promise clause emphasizes the assertion; the intervening time phrase makes the repetition apt, and makhrujūn predicates the first clause.
RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r1.anchor: ثنى إنكم للتوكيد وحسن ذلك الفصل

RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿūd's reading omits the intervening phrase about dying and being dust and bones.
RAZI-FULL:v23p86/r2.anchor: وفي قراءة ابن مسعود : { وكنتم ترابا

STUDYQURAN:23:35/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:35/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:35/r1.claim: The objection that humans reduced to dust and bones can be revived recurs in the cited verses; revival of dead bones is also discussed in two other contexts.
STUDYQURAN:23:35/r1.anchor: The notion of the revival of human beings who have become mere dust and bones, usually invoked in the form of an objection posed by those who balk at the possibility of bodily resurrection

STUDYQURAN:23:35/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:35/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:35/r2.claim: “Brought forth” literally means “caused to leave it”: the dead leave the earth where they lie when given life on the Last Day.
STUDYQURAN:23:35/r2.anchor: Brought forth is literally “caused to leave [it]”, meaning caused to leave the earth in which they lie when they are given life on the Last Day

TABRISI:23:35/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:35/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:35/r12.claim: The author reports that Sibawayh treats the second anna in this and two other cited constructions as appositive to the first.
TABRISI:23:35/r12.anchor: اختلفوا في أن الثانية من قوله سبحانه

TABRISI:23:35/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:35/r13.speaker: أبو عمرو الجرمي، المبرد
TABRISI:23:35/r13.claim: Abu Amr al-Jurmi and al-Mubarrad treat the second anna as repetition for emphasis and because of the construction’s length.
TABRISI:23:35/r13.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو الجرمي وأبو العباس المبرد: إنها مكررة للتأكيد وطول الكلام

TABRISI:23:35/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:35/r14.speaker: أبو الحسن
TABRISI:23:35/r14.claim: Abu al-Hasan says the second anna is raised by the adverb; Abu Ali al-Farisi chooses it and refutes the other two.
TABRISI:23:35/r14.anchor: وقال أبو الحسن: إنها مرتفع بالظرف واختاره أبو علي الفارسي وزيف القولين

TABRISI:23:35/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:35/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:35/r15.claim: On Sibawayh’s analysis, the first anna clause is the second object of promise: extraction is promised after death, when they have become dust and bones.
TABRISI:23:35/r15.anchor: إن أن الأولى في قوله أيعدكم أنكم مع اسمها وخبرها في موضع نصب على أنه المفعول الثاني من الوعد

TABRISI:23:35/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:35/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:35/r16.claim: On the repetition analysis, the construction means he promises they will be brought out after death.
TABRISI:23:35/r16.anchor: وأما على مذهب من جعله للتكرير فتقديره أيعدكم أنكم بعد موتكم مخرجون

TABRISI:23:31-40/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:31-40/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:31-40/r1.claim: On Abu al-Hasan and Abu Ali’s analysis, the second anna clause is raised by the adverb and functions as the first clause’s predicate.
TABRISI:23:31-40/r1.anchor: وأما على مذهب أبي الحسن وأبي علي فتقديره أيعدكم أنكم إذا متم إخراجكم

TABRISI:23:31-40/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:31-40/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:31-40/r2.claim: The adverb cannot be governed by extraction itself, because that would leave the sentence incomplete; an implicit event or verb supplies its governor.
TABRISI:23:31-40/r2.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يكون العامل فيه الإخراج نفسه إذ لو كان كذلك لكان الكلام غير تام

TABRISI:23:31-40/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:31-40/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:31-40/r3.claim: The syntax has an implicit event such as happens or is, with the adverb replacing it and raising the subject, as in “Zayd went” or “Zayd is going.”
TABRISI:23:31-40/r3.anchor: والعامل في الظرف في الأصل الفعل المحذوف أو معنى الفعل مثل قولك يحدث أو حادث

TABRISI:23:31-40/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:31-40/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:31-40/r4.claim: Underlying wording can be “when you die, your extraction happens”; eliding the verb lets idha stand in its place and raise “you will be extracted.”
TABRISI:23:31-40/r4.anchor: فكذلك إذا في الآية تقديره في الأصل إذا متم إخراجكم كائن أو حادث

TABRISI:23:31-40/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:31-40/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:31-40/r5.claim: Alternatively, “you will be extracted” occupies the conditional answer position, with an implicit event governing idha.
TABRISI:23:31-40/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن نقول إن الاسم الذي هو إنكم مخرجون واقع موقع جواب شرط إذا

TABRISI:23:31-40/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:31-40/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:31-40/r6.claim: The commentary does not repeat how the other two cited verses raise second anna by the adverb, since the explanation was given earlier.
TABRISI:23:31-40/r6.anchor: فأما تقدير ارتفاع أن الثانية بالظرف في الآيتين الأخيرتين فقد تقدم بيانه

TABRISI:23:31-40/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:31-40/r7.speaker: أبو عثمان
TABRISI:23:31-40/r7.claim: Abu Uthman and others allow an implicit adverb to govern a noun, as with “their like” in al-Farazdaq’s verse.
TABRISI:23:31-40/r7.anchor: فقد أجاز أبو عثمان وغيره إضمار الظرف وإعماله كما قالوا في انتصاب مثلهم في بيت الفرزدق

TABRISI:23:35-40/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:35-40/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:35-40/r1.claim: The al-Farazdaq line is analyzed with an implicit adverb governing “their like.”
TABRISI:23:35-40/r1.anchor: إذ هم قريش وإذ ما مثلهم بشر أنه على ظرف مضمر

TABRISI:23:35-40/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:35-40/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:35-40/r11.claim: The person promising resurrection is the messenger.

TABRISI:23:35-40/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:35-40/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:35-40/r12.claim: They decay after death, and the promised extraction is being brought alive from their graves.
TABRISI:23:35-40/r12.anchor: وصرتم بعد الموت رميما { أنكم مخرجون } من قبوركم أحياء

TABRISI:39:17-19/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:39:17-19/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:39:17-19/r6.claim: The repeated ‘that’ in 23:35 illustrates the same construction; alternatively, an omitted predicate asks whether the condemned can escape, with the implied answer that none can rescue him.
TABRISI:39:17-19/r6.anchor: أيعدكم أنكم إذا متم وكنتم ترابا وعظاما أنكم مخرجرن

THALABI:v7p46/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p46/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p46/r6.claim: They deny that people will emerge alive from their graves after death and after flesh has disappeared, leaving dust and bones.
THALABI:v7p46/r6.anchor: قد ذهبت اللحوم أنكم مخرجون من قبوركم أحياء

THALABI:v7p46/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p46/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p46/r7.claim: The clause repeats innakum after the long intervening phrase because the speech has become extended.
THALABI:v7p46/r7.anchor: وأعاد إنكم لما طال الكلام، ومعنى وكنتم ترابا وعظاما إنكم مخرجون .

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p564#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p564#2/r2.speaker: عبد الله
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p564#2/r2.claim: The repeated أن has one sense, and the separation by إذا makes the repetition sound well-formed; Abdullah’s reading has only one أن after إذا.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p564#2/r2.anchor: قال الفراء: أعيدت (أنكم) مرتين ومعناهما واحد، إلا أن ذلك حسن لما فرق بينهما بإذا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p564#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p564#2/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p564#2/r3.claim: Abu Ishaq parses the first أنكم as an object of promise, conventionally with an understood ب; some treat the second أن as occupying the same position and repeated for emphasis, yielding the sense that resurrection follows death. He compares 9:63.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p564#2/r3.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: {أنكم} موضعها نصب على معنى: أيعدكم بأنكم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p564#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p564#2/r4.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p564#2/r4.claim: Abu Ali lists analyses of the second أن: apposition, emphasis, an uncounted extra particle, or being raised by the adverb. Sibawayh chooses apposition, Abu al-Abbas and al-Jarmi emphasis, and Abu al-Hasan the adverbial analysis; no one endorses the extra-particle view.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p564#2/r4.anchor: قال أبو علي الفارسي: لا يخلو (أن) الثانية في قوله: {أيعدكم أنكم} الآية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p564#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p564#2/r5.speaker: سيبويه
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p564#2/r5.claim: Sibawayh treats the second أن as replacing the first: the intended sense is that you will be brought out when you die, with the first particle placed early to signal what precedes resurrection.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p564#2/r5.anchor: فمذهب (¬7) سيبويه (¬8): أن الثانية بدل من الأولى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p564#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p564#2/r6.speaker: أبو الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p564#2/r6.claim: Abu al-Hasan says the second أن is raised by the adverbial phrase.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p564#2/r6.anchor: ومذهب أبي الحسن (¬10) أنه مرتفع بالظرف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p564#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p564#2/r7.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p564#2/r7.claim: Abu Ali notes that no one considered the second particle an extra element to be disregarded.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p564#2/r7.anchor: ولم يقل أحد أنه زائد غير معتد به

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p566/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p566/r1.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p566/r1.claim: Abu Ali rejects Sibawayh’s apposition analysis: the first أن is not complete before إذا متم, and that time clause cannot be a predicate of the addressed persons; the parallel conditional in 9:63 also cannot complete the first clause.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p566/r1.anchor: قال أبو على: لا يجوز عندي (¬4) أن تكون (أن) الثانية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p566/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p566/r2.speaker: أبو العباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p566/r2.claim: Abu al-Abbas calls repetition of the second أن the best account, since it means the same as the first; Abu Ali says even this fails because the particle cannot be repeated without its clause.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p566/r2.anchor: وأبو العباس يذهب إلى أن الثانية مكررة توكيدا، ولست تريد بها إلا ما أردت بالأولى. قال (¬5): وهذا أحسن الأقاويل عندي في هذه الآية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p566/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p566/r3.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p566/r3.claim: Abu Ali rejects Abu al-Abbas’s emphasis analysis: one cannot repeat أن alone without its clause, and the first clause has not completed its complement; he says it remains closer than apposition.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p566/r3.anchor: فلا يجوز التكرير (¬8) فيها وحدها، كما لا تكرر سائر الموصولات دون

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p566/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p566/r4.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p566/r4.claim: Abu Ali concludes that the second أن is raised by the overt ظرف إذا: the clause from إذا متم through مخرجون serves as the first أن’s predicate, with the sense that resurrection is at the time of death.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p566/r4.anchor: ثبت أنها مرتفعة بالظرف الظاهر الذي هو (إذا)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p570/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p570/r1.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p570/r1.claim: Those who defend apposition may posit an omitted إخراجكم, making extraction at death a complete predicate; a time phrase can predicate an event, unlike the persons addressed. Those who defend repetition need no omitted word.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p570/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p570/r2.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p570/r2.claim: Abu Ali argues وعد takes two direct objects, so the first أنكم can be accusative as the second object without an implied ب, as Quranic usage shows at 48:20, 20:80, 7:142, 48:29, and 9:114.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p570/r2.anchor: قال: فأما (¬4) قول أبي إسحاق {أيعدكم أنكم} إن موضع (أن) الأولى نصب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p570/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p570/r3.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p570/r3.claim: The Quranic examples show وعد takes its second object without a preposition, so no حرف الخفض need be supplied in this verse.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v15p570/r3.anchor: ولا حاجة إلى تقدير الباء ألا ترى أن ما جاء في التنزيل من هذا بغير الباء

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:35-37/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:35-37/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:23:35-37/r1.claim: Being brought out means being raised alive from the graves.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p400#2/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p400#2/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p400#2/r2.claim: The question is spoken by some chiefs to one another.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p400#2/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p400#2/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p400#2/r3.claim: They mock the promise that people will be brought out after death and decay, denying resurrection.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p400#2/r3.anchor: مبعوثون. أي قد وعدكم ذلك، تكذبون بالبعث

ELMALILI:23:31-41/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:23:31-41/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:23:31-41/r8.claim: The people dismiss bodily resurrection from dust and bones as impossibly remote, claim worldly life is all there is, and say one generation dies as another is born, so they should enjoy this low life.
ELMALILI:23:31-41/r8.anchor: kimimiz bir taraftan ölür, kimimiz de yeni doğar hayata geliriz, böyle gider

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r5.claim: Opponents of prophets were often wealthy elites content with the order because it served their interests; they feared afterlife accountability and a society conscious of universal rights and justice would threaten their status.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r5.anchor: bunlar umumiyetle hak peygamberin getirdiği sistemi kendi toplumsal ve ekonomik statüleri için tehlikeli görmüşler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r7.claim: Since the Qur’an answers these denials of the prophet’s person and of the afterlife elsewhere, this passage only warns of the rejecters’ painful fate.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:31/r7.anchor: burada bir defa daha tekrarlanmasına gerek görülmemiş, sadece uğrayacakları acı âkıbete dikkat çekilmekle yetinilmiştir

ITQAN:v3p177/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p177/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p177/r5.claim: Literal repetition emphasizes nouns, clauses, verbs, imperative nouns, and particles; examples include qawārīr qawārīr, dakkan dakka, amhilhum, hayhāta, and repeated anna or fī.
ITQAN:v3p177/r5.anchor: وإما بلفظه ويكون في الاسم والفعل والحرف والجملة

BURHAN:v4p165/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p165/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p165/r6.claim: If the second ‘that’ is appositional, an omitted ‘intending’ must be supplied to complete the clause and make the time phrase a predicate; the alternative parse needs no supplement.
BURHAN:v4p165/r6.anchor: فمن قدر في أن الثانية البدل فينبغي أن يقدر محذوفا ليتم الكلام فيصح البدل

BURHAN:v3p13/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p13/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p13/r3.claim: When long discourse may cause an earlier point to be forgotten, repetition renews it; he illustrates this with repeated clauses and pronouns.
BURHAN:v3p13/r3.anchor: إذا طال الكلام وخشى تناسى الأول أعيد ثانيا تطرية له وتجديدا لعهده

BURHAN:v3p13/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p13/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p13/r4.claim: The second إنكم builds on the first and guards against forgetting it.
BURHAN:v3p13/r4.anchor: الثاني بناء على الأول إذ كارا به خشية تناسيه

BURHAN:v2p386/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p386/r8.speaker: الكوفيون
BURHAN:v2p386/r8.claim: The Kūfans say an emphatic element cannot be separated from what it emphasizes; al-Ṣaffār rejects this against transmitted usage, citing pronouns, repeated لما, and repeated أنكم.
BURHAN:v2p386/r8.anchor: وزعم الكوفيون انه لا يجوز الفصل بين التوكيد المؤكد قال الصفار في شرح سيبويه والسماع يرده
